title: Soft-deadline streaming session handshake, per-chunk retries, and resume semantics for Go SDK
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
The current Go SDK streaming primitives expose raw context cancellation and a single hard deadline propagation. In practice customers want: (1) a soft-deadline (best-effort) per-session signal that prefers fast graceful shutdown but allows in-flight token completion, (2) per-chunk soft timeouts with limited per-chunk retries, and (3) a resume handshake so clients can reconnect and continue a stream with minimal duplication. This ticket defines an implementation that balances ergonomics, safety, and compatibility with the hosted runtime.

Goals:
- Add a session-level ‘SoftDeadline’ signal that can be checked by user code and the SDK runtime; it triggers graceful flush/final-token semantics rather than abrupt cancellation.
- Implement per-chunk soft timeouts with configurable retry (N=0..3), jittered backoff, and idempotency markers to avoid duplicate side effects.
- Define a compact resume handshake flow (ResumeToken + last-offset ack) that the Go SDK exposes with examples.
- Keep the existing Stream API backward compatible; new features are opt-in via options struct.

Non-goals:
- Full on-disk checkpointing for long-lived streams (out of scope for this ticket).

Proposal (high-level):
- API: Introduce StreamOptions struct: SoftDeadline time.Duration, ChunkTimeout time.Duration, ChunkRetries int, ResumeWindow time.Duration. Add methods StreamWithOptions(ctx, req, opts) and StreamResume(ctx, resumeToken, opts).
- Runtime behavior: SoftDeadline causes the SDK to set an HTTP header X-Soft-Deadline and prefer traceable end-of-stream flush frames. ChunkTimeout triggers a per-chunk timer; on expiry SDK attempts a fast retry up to ChunkRetries with exponential backoff (base 100ms, jitter 0-30%). Each chunk uses an Idempotency-Key derived from sessionID+chunkIndex so server-side duplicate suppression is possible.
- Resume handshake: server may return Resume-Token and Last-Acked-Chunk. On reconnection client calls StreamResume with token+lastAck; server will stream remaining chunks from lastAck+1. If token is stale server returns 410 and client should fall back to new session semantics.
- Context interaction: Hard context cancellation still immediately closes gRPC/HTTP connection. SoftDeadline is advisory: SDK tries to finish the current token and send a final flush frame but will abort if a hard context cancel arrives.
- Observability: Emit SDK events via Redwood Console traces: soft_deadline_triggered, chunk_retry, resume_attempt, resume_failed. Include per-chunk latency and retry counts.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- Default StreamWithOptions uses zero values so behavior is identical to current Stream.
- Add examples in docs and README showing how to opt-in and the recommended defaults (ChunkTimeout=2s, ChunkRetries=1, SoftDeadline=250ms).

Acceptance criteria:
- API compiled and unit tests for options parsing and header behavior.
- Integration test against staging runtime exercising soft-deadline flush, chunk retries (simulate transient 503 on one chunk), and resume flow (simulate connection drop, reconnect with token, verify no data duplication).
- End-to-end perf: <5% additional median latency with default options enabled, and failure cost bounded by configured ChunkRetries.
- Docs and Go example: two idiomatic snippets (simple graceful shutdown and resume example) checked into docs/ and linked to SDK README.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Introducing idempotency markers requires server support (coordination with runtime). We'll gate the feature: server ignores markers if not supported.
- SoftDeadline is advisory and might be confusing; docs must be explicit about difference from ctx.Deadline.
- More timers per chunk increases goroutine/timer pressure; implementation will reuse a pooled timer wheel to avoid proliferation.

Open questions:
- Should ChunkRetries be per-chunk or per-request-window? Current proposal uses per-chunk.
- What should the default resume token TTL be? Proposal: 5 minutes.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) API shape and unit tests (this ticket): add StreamOptions, compile.
2) Low-level runtime: per-chunk timers, idempotency-key plumbing, header propagation.
3) Resume handshake client code + mock server responses for integration tests.
4) Integration tests in staging + observability events wired.
5) Docs, examples, and a small alpha release.

References:
- Design doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/go-sdk-streaming-soft-deadline (internal)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/512 (WIP)
- Runtime issue tracking server support: ENG-811002 (server resume token support)
comments: 2026-02-22 - Marco Li: Spike completed for timer-wheel reuse. Implemented a pooled timer abstraction, benchmarked with 10k concurrent streams. Memory regression <5%. See branch spike/timer-wheel.

2026-02-26 - Rebecca Owens (PM): Reviewed API surface. Requested defaults that bias low-latency: ChunkTimeout=2s, ChunkRetries=1, SoftDeadline=150ms. Also asked for a clear UX note that SoftDeadline != ctx.Deadline.
2026-03-01 - Dmitri Ivanov (SRE): Observability hooks proposed look good. Added request to emit explicit counter for chunk_retries_total and a tag for session_id.

2026-03-05 - Marco Li: Implemented idempotency-key generator (sessionID:uuid + chunkIndex) and header propagation. Unit tests added for header presence and derivation. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/512

2026-03-08 - Aisha Patel: Integration notes from staging run: chunk retry path recovered correctly for simulated transient 502s, but resume handshake failed when resume token TTL was set to 30s. Increasing TTL to 5 minutes fixed most flakes. Logging added to help debug stale tokens.

2026-03-10 - Marco Li: Marking this ticket In Progress -> still need to add docs and final integration test asserting no-duplication semantics. Planned work this week: add README example + run the full e2e suite against staging runtime-2026.03-alpha.
